diff --git a/debian/patches/riscv64-keep-heap-allocations-within-reach-of-the-loaded-image.patch b/debian/patches/riscv64-keep-heap-allocations-within-reach-of-the-loaded-image.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..3989e73
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/riscv64-keep-heap-allocations-within-reach-of-the-loaded-image.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,167 @@
+From: Valentin Haudiquet <valentin.haudiquet@canonical.com>
+Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:25:22 +0100
+Subject: riscv64: keep heap allocations within reach of the loaded image
+
+When built with -mcmodel=medany, GRUB modules call into the kernel and
+into each other through PC-relative relocations: on riscv64, the
+R_RISCV_CALL/R_RISCV_PCREL_HI20 families encode a signed 32-bit
+displacement, so a module loaded more than 2GiB away from the code it
+calls cannot be relocated, and module loading fails with "relocation
+overflow". GCC supports -mcmodel=large on riscv64 since GCC 14; with
+older compilers, configure falls back to -mcmodel=medany. Builds using
+-mcmodel=large are not affected, as their modules only use absolute
+relocations.
+
+grub_efi_mm_add_regions() currently picks heap regions from the
+largest free EFI memory blocks, without regard to where the firmware
+loaded the GRUB image. On a riscv64 server (PXE boot) the firmware
+loads the image just below 4GiB (0xf4000000), while the largest free
+block in its EFI memory map sits at 0xc010000000 (about 45GiB away)
+and the first module load aborts.
+
+When sorting the memory map for heap allocation, prefer regions
+within a window around the loaded image. As modules relocate against
+each other as well as against the kernel, the image and the whole
+heap must fit within the reach of a single relocation, so the window
+spans 2GiB, minus a 1MiB margin, centred on the image. In-window
+regions are still sorted largest first, and out-of-window regions
+follow them.
+
+If the loaded-image protocol is unavailable, the window degenerates
+to the whole address space and behaviour is unchanged.
+
+Signed-off-by: Valentin Haudiquet <valentin.haudiquet@canonical.com>
+
+---
+diff --git a/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c b/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c
+index df238b165..75fb7d2dd 100644
+--- a/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c
++++ b/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c
+@@ -403,6 +403,56 @@ grub_efi_get_memory_map (grub_efi_uintn_t *memory_map_size,
+     return -1;
+ }
+ 
++#ifdef GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH
++/* Keep the window this far from the edge of the relocation reach, so
++   that offsets stay clear of the rounding of HI20/LO12 pairs.  */
++#define HEAP_WINDOW_MARGIN	0x100000
++
++static grub_addr_t heap_window_lo, heap_window_hi;
++static int heap_window_valid;
++
++/* Compute, once, the window [*LO, *HI) where the heap is preferably
++   allocated.  Modules call into the kernel and into each other, so
++   the image and the whole heap must fit within the reach of a single
++   relocation: the window is centred on the loaded image and spans
++   GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH minus a margin.  Both edges are
++   page-aligned.  Without the loaded-image protocol, or with an image
++   too large to leave room around it, the window is unrestricted.  */
++static void
++grub_efi_heap_bounds (grub_addr_t *lo, grub_addr_t *hi)
++{
++  grub_efi_loaded_image_t *image;
++  grub_addr_t base, end, span, slack;
++
++  if (heap_window_valid)
++    goto out;
++
++  heap_window_lo = 0;
++  heap_window_hi = ~(grub_addr_t) 0;
++  heap_window_valid = 1;
++
++  image = grub_efi_get_loaded_image (grub_efi_image_handle);
++  if (! image)
++    goto out;
++
++  base = (grub_addr_t) image->image_base;
++  end = base + (grub_addr_t) image->image_size;
++  span = GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH - HEAP_WINDOW_MARGIN;
++  if (image->image_size >= span)
++    goto out;
++
++  slack = (span - image->image_size) / 2;
++  heap_window_lo = base > slack ? base - slack : 0;
++  heap_window_hi = end > ~(grub_addr_t) 0 - slack ? ~(grub_addr_t) 0 : end + slack;
++  heap_window_lo = ALIGN_UP (heap_window_lo, GRUB_EFI_PAGE_SIZE);
++  heap_window_hi = ALIGN_DOWN (heap_window_hi, GRUB_EFI_PAGE_SIZE);
++
++ out:
++  *lo = heap_window_lo;
++  *hi = heap_window_hi;
++}
++#endif
++
+ /* Sort the memory map in place.  */
+ static void
+ sort_memory_map (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+@@ -411,6 +461,13 @@ sort_memory_map (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+ {
+   grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *d1;
+   grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *d2;
++#ifdef GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH
++  grub_addr_t heap_lo, heap_hi;
++
++  grub_efi_heap_bounds (&heap_lo, &heap_hi);
++  grub_dprintf ("mm", "heap window [0x%" PRIxGRUB_ADDR ", 0x%" PRIxGRUB_ADDR ")\n",
++		heap_lo, heap_hi);
++#endif
+ 
+   for (d1 = memory_map;
+        d1 < memory_map_end;
+@@ -422,6 +479,29 @@ sort_memory_map (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+ 	   d2 < memory_map_end;
+ 	   d2 = NEXT_MEMORY_DESCRIPTOR (d2, desc_size))
+ 	{
++#ifdef GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH
++	  /* Keep regions overlapping the window ahead of the ones
++	     outside it; within each group, order by size as before.
++	     Out-of-window regions are still used when the window does
++	     not contain enough free memory.  */
++	  {
++	    int max_in = ((grub_addr_t) max_desc->physical_start
++			  + PAGES_TO_BYTES (max_desc->num_pages) > heap_lo
++			  && (grub_addr_t) max_desc->physical_start < heap_hi);
++	    int d2_in = ((grub_addr_t) d2->physical_start
++			 + PAGES_TO_BYTES (d2->num_pages) > heap_lo
++			 && (grub_addr_t) d2->physical_start < heap_hi);
++
++	    if (max_in && ! d2_in)
++	      continue;
++	    if (! max_in && d2_in)
++	      {
++		max_desc = d2;
++		continue;
++	      }
++	  }
++#endif
++
+ 	  if (max_desc->num_pages < d2->num_pages)
+ 	    max_desc = d2;
+ 	}
+@@ -524,7 +604,6 @@ add_memory_regions (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+ 	return grub_error (GRUB_ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY,
+ 			    "Memory starting at %p (%u pages) marked as free, but EFI would not allocate",
+ 			    (void *) ((grub_addr_t) start), (unsigned) pages);
+-
+       grub_mm_init_region (addr, PAGES_TO_BYTES (pages));
+ 
+       required_pages -= pages;
+diff --git a/include/grub/riscv64/efi/memory.h b/include/grub/riscv64/efi/memory.h
+index c6cb32417..e6a9a367f 100644
+--- a/include/grub/riscv64/efi/memory.h
++++ b/include/grub/riscv64/efi/memory.h
+@@ -1,6 +1,14 @@
+ #ifndef GRUB_MEMORY_CPU_HEADER
+ #include <grub/efi/memory.h>
+ 
++/* With -mcmodel=medany, modules reach kernel and other module symbols
++   through PC-relative relocations (R_RISCV_CALL, R_RISCV_PCREL_HI20)
++   with a signed 32-bit reach, so the image and the whole heap must fit
++   in a 2GiB span.  -mcmodel=large uses absolute addresses instead.  */
++#ifdef __riscv_cmodel_medany
++#define GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH 0x80000000ULL
++#endif
++
+ #define GRUB_EFI_MAX_USABLE_ADDRESS 0xffffffffffffULL
+ 
+ #endif /* ! GRUB_MEMORY_CPU_HEADER */
diff --git a/debian/patches/riscv64-split-heap-regions-at-the-edges-of-the-relocation-window.patch b/debian/patches/riscv64-split-heap-regions-at-the-edges-of-the-relocation-window.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9cca47f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/riscv64-split-heap-regions-at-the-edges-of-the-relocation-window.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+From: Valentin Haudiquet <valentin.haudiquet@canonical.com>
+Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:41:14 +0100
+Subject: [PATCH 2/2] riscv64: split heap regions at the edges of the
+ relocation window
+
+Heap regions are picked from the sorted regions of the filtered EFI
+memory map, so a region that only partially overlaps the heap
+allocation window around the loaded image can contribute pages out
+of reach of the image even though the sort prefers it: a region
+extending past an edge of the window carries out-of-window pages at
+the edge the heap is carved from, and the heap only falls back to
+other regions once it is exhausted.
+
+Split every region crossing an edge of the window while filtering
+the memory map, so that each emitted descriptor is either wholly
+in-window or wholly outside it: the sort then prefers the true
+in-window extent of the region, and the parts outside remain
+available as fallbacks when the window does not contain enough
+free memory.  As regions do not overlap, at most one region
+straddles each edge, so at most two extra descriptors are emitted;
+the filtered map buffer already reserves headroom for many more.
+
+The window edges are page-aligned, so every emitted descriptor stays
+page-aligned and can be passed to AllocatePages().
+
+Signed-off-by: Valentin Haudiquet <valentin.haudiquet@canonical.com>
+---
+ grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c | 61 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
+ 1 file changed, 61 insertions(+)
+
+diff --git a/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c b/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c
+index fad53be69..e6ddc54a8 100644
+--- a/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c
++++ b/grub-core/kern/efi/mm.c
+@@ -527,6 +527,57 @@ sort_memory_map (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+     }
+ }
+ 
++#ifdef GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH
++/* Split DESC in place at the edges of the heap allocation window
++   [LO, HI), so that every resulting descriptor is either wholly
++   in-window or wholly outside it.  The sort can then prefer the
++   in-window part of the region and keep the parts outside as
++   fallbacks.  The in-window part stays at DESC, the parts below
++   and above the window follow it.  Return the position where the
++   next descriptor is to be written.
++
++   A region crossing no edge is left as is.  Regions do not
++   overlap, so at most one region crosses each edge and at most
++   two extra descriptors are written per memory map.  */
++static grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *
++split_descriptor_at_window (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *desc,
++			    grub_efi_uintn_t desc_size,
++			    grub_addr_t lo,
++			    grub_addr_t hi)
++{
++  grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t orig = *desc;
++  grub_addr_t start = orig.physical_start;
++  grub_addr_t end = start + PAGES_TO_BYTES (orig.num_pages);
++  grub_addr_t in_start, in_end;
++
++  if (end <= lo || start >= hi || (start >= lo && end <= hi))
++    return NEXT_MEMORY_DESCRIPTOR (desc, desc_size);
++
++  in_start = start > lo ? start : lo;
++  in_end = end < hi ? end : hi;
++
++  desc->physical_start = in_start;
++  desc->num_pages = BYTES_TO_PAGES_DOWN (in_end - in_start);
++  desc = NEXT_MEMORY_DESCRIPTOR (desc, desc_size);
++
++  if (start < in_start)
++    {
++      *desc = orig;
++      desc->num_pages = BYTES_TO_PAGES_DOWN (in_start - start);
++      desc = NEXT_MEMORY_DESCRIPTOR (desc, desc_size);
++    }
++  if (end > in_end)
++    {
++      *desc = orig;
++      desc->physical_start = in_end;
++      desc->num_pages = BYTES_TO_PAGES_DOWN (end - in_end);
++      desc = NEXT_MEMORY_DESCRIPTOR (desc, desc_size);
++    }
++
++  return desc;
++}
++#endif
++
+ /* Filter the descriptors. GRUB needs only available memory.  */
+ static grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *
+ filter_memory_map (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+@@ -536,6 +587,11 @@ filter_memory_map (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+ {
+   grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *desc;
+   grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *filtered_desc;
++#ifdef GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH
++  grub_addr_t heap_lo, heap_hi;
++
++  grub_efi_heap_bounds (&heap_lo, &heap_hi);
++#endif
+ 
+   for (desc = memory_map, filtered_desc = filtered_memory_map;
+        desc < memory_map_end;
+@@ -570,7 +626,12 @@ filter_memory_map (grub_efi_memory_descriptor_t *memory_map,
+ 	  if (filtered_desc->num_pages == 0)
+ 	    continue;
+ 
++#ifdef GRUB_EFI_HEAP_RELOCATION_REACH
++	  filtered_desc = split_descriptor_at_window (filtered_desc, desc_size,
++						      heap_lo, heap_hi);
++#else
+ 	  filtered_desc = NEXT_MEMORY_DESCRIPTOR (filtered_desc, desc_size);
++#endif
+ 	}
+     }
+ 
+-- 
+GitLab
+
+
